import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/training_9.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first numerical index column
    dfs.append(df)

# All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
# ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, since schemas are identical, we UNION all source tables.

# Concatenate all dataframes (union)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the target schema and types:
target_df = target_df.astype({
    'admit': 'int64',
    'gre': 'int64',
    'gpa': 'float64',
    'prestige': 'int64'
})

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_83/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
